problem: A 12-byte routine starting at 000BH ends at 0016H, so it overwrites four bytes, 0013H to 0016H, not just 0013H and 0014H. The conclusion is right but the address detail is wrong and would mislead a student counting bytes.
fix: A 12-byte ISR at 000BH runs from 000BH to 0016H, so it overwrites the INT1 vector slot (0013H to 001AH) and the program will crash or jump wrongly on an INT1 request. Put SJMP/LJMP at 000BH to a routine placed elsewhere.

problem: The caption explains only the accent and live marks on the Vector row; the spec also puts a 'next' mark on the Source row at index 1 (T0), which the caption never mentions, so the reader cannot tell what that highlight means.
fix: Either drop the '1': 'next' mark from the Source row, or extend the caption to say the Timer 0 source is highlighted as the next topic to trace through the table.

problem: The section explains which source wins when two requests arrive together, but never states the pre-emption rule: a high-priority request interrupts a running low-priority ISR, while a same-priority request must wait. Interrupt programming depends on this.
fix: Add: a high-priority request pre-empts a low-priority ISR in progress; a new request of the same or lower priority waits until the current ISR ends with RETI. High-priority ISRs therefore must be short.
